body.justification: The exact factorization identifies precisely what information the pilot contains and exposes the missing deterministic-array information limit.
body.gap: Armstrong's Gaussian-shift efficiency conclusions require average-information convergence, and no current exact-rerandomization result supplies the subsequent finite-action transfer.
body.consumer: Future work can test the score-information condition separately from the lattice-boundary condition before reporting a nuisance-efficient pilot value.
body.proof_tex:
The pilot split and its balanced complete randomization are parameter-free.  The baseline law is the point mass at \(\mathbf X_n\) by \(\mathrm{ass{:}fixed\text{-}baseline}\), and conditional outcomes are independent by \(\mathrm{ass{:}stable\text{-}product\text{-}law}\).  Consequently the factors for \(S_m\), \(Z_{S_m}\), and \(\mathbf X_n\) cancel from the likelihood ratio, while unobserved potential outcomes integrate to one.  What remains is
\[
\frac{dP_{\beta+v/\sqrt m}^{\mathcal O_m}}
{dP_{\beta}^{\mathcal O_m}}
=\prod_{i\in S_m}
\frac{p_{Z_i,\beta+v/\sqrt m}(Y_{in}(Z_i)\mid x_{in})}
{p_{Z_i,\beta}(Y_{in}(Z_i)\mid x_{in})},
\]
and taking logarithms proves the first display.  Quadratic-mean differentiability identifies the conditional score central sequence as
\[
\Delta_m(\beta)=m^{-1/2}\sum_{i\in S_m}
s_{Z_i,\beta}(Y_{in}(Z_i)\mid x_{in}).
\]
Each summand has conditional mean zero, and the product law makes distinct summands conditionally independent.  Therefore
\[
\operatorname{Var}_\beta\{\Delta_m(\beta)\mid S_m,Z_{S_m},\mathbf X_n\}
=\frac1m\sum_{i\in S_m}
E_\beta(s_{Z_i,\beta}s_{Z_i,\beta}^{\mathsf T}\mid x_{in})
=\mathcal I_m(\beta;S_m,Z_{S_m}),
\]
which proves the information identity.

We now give an explicit certificate that convergence to \(I(\beta)\) is not implied.  Take \(p=1\), let \(\nu\) be Lebesgue measure on \([0,1]\), and choose an equidistributed triangular array consisting entirely of rational points.  It is bounded, converges weakly to \(\nu\), and can be chosen with empirical variance bounded away from zero.  Define the bounded measurable function
\[
h(x)=1+\mathbf 1\{x\in\mathbb Q\}.
\]
Choose distinct bounded support points \(y_1,\ldots,y_J\), strictly positive probabilities \(p_1^0,\ldots,p_J^0\), and a nonzero vector \(v=(v_1,\ldots,v_J)\) satisfying
\[
\sum_{j=1}^Jv_j=\sum_{j=1}^Jy_jv_j
=\sum_{j=1}^Jy_j^2v_j=0.
\tag{10}
\]
For example, for \((-2,-1,0,1,2)\) one may take \(v=(1,-4,6,-4,1)\).  For \(|\theta|\) in a sufficiently small compact interval, set
\[
p_{q,\theta}(y_j\mid x)=p_j^0+\theta h(x)v_j
\qquad(q\in\mathcal Q).
\tag{11}
\]
Positivity follows by shrinking the interval.  Equation (10) makes the first two conditional moments in (11) constant in \((x,\theta)\), so all stated moment-smoothness conditions hold.  Finite support and uniform positivity give uniform quadratic-mean differentiability and bounded third score moments.  At \(\theta=0\), however,
\[
E_0\{s_{q,0}^2\mid x\}
=h(x)^2\sum_{j=1}^J\frac{v_j^2}{p_j^0}.
\tag{12}
\]
Because every array point is rational, the empirical average of (12) equals four times the constant on the right without \(h(x)^2\), whereas its \(\nu\)-integral equals that constant because the rationals have Lebesgue measure zero.  Balanced assignment and uniform sampling of the pilot do not remove this discrepancy: the corresponding entry of \(\mathcal I_m\) converges in probability to four times the corresponding entry of \(I(0)\).

The construction can be embedded in the full regular chart by taking further linearly independent finite-support perturbation directions.  The direction (10) may be assigned to a nuisance coordinate, so it changes neither the first two moments nor \(G_T\); a regular oracle-coordinate block can therefore retain the oracle-smoothness, rank, signal, and curvature conditions.  If necessary, the same zero-moment perturbation may instead be added to a regular oracle score direction without changing its moment derivatives.  Thus the missing score-information convergence is not a consequence of the remaining model conditions.  Without that convergence, quadratic-mean differentiability does not identify the experiment with the Gaussian shift having information \(I(\beta)\), and neither nuisance-efficient covariance \(I_{\mathrm{eff}}^{-1}\) nor a decision-theoretic action bound with constant \(B(\beta)\) follows.  The additional exact finite-boundary transfer is separately posed in \(\mathrm{oeq{:}finite\text{-}boundary\text{-}comparison}\).
